I suspect they would find similar. I also have problems with studies like this because they imply a causation effect by correlation. People take meds because a problem starts. Most meds treat symptoms, not the real problems (Someone might be taking a PPI for GERD, but it is caused by binge drinking-since Alcohol relaxes the upper sphincter. Things like that.).

Maybe I just have some bias going on towards studies based in statistical significance. To me that just says it needs to be looked into more. Not declared sound by its own merit.

Also Calcium would reduce PH short term-but the stomach interprets that as a shortage and cranks up acid production-it's what makes drinking milk or eating yogurt while having an ulcer bad.
